# Purpose

Support student work that connects the maintenance-access context to combined loading. Award credit for a defensible idealization, correct support reactions, internal axial force, transverse shear force and bending moment, valid rectangular-section properties, normal-stress superposition, transverse shear stress at point A, a complete differential stress element, and an appropriately limited engineering assessment.

# Scope of the Base Problem

The base model assumes static loading, a straight prismatic member, a concentrated technician load, negligible member self-weight, small deformation, linear-elastic stress relations, smooth contact at C, and two reaction components at B. It neglects local contact, impact, vibration, fatigue, instability, connection details, and material nonlinearity.

Point A is located at y_A = t/4 above the centroidal neutral axis so that the selected point has nonzero axial normal stress, bending normal stress, and transverse shear stress. The section appearance is schematic, and no material property is required for the assigned stress calculation.

# Supplemental Assessment Structure

- context interpretation and load path: 20%;
- idealization, boundary conditions, and assumptions: 20%;
- equilibrium and internal resultants: 25%;
- combined-stress calculations: 25%;
- stress element and engineering assessment: 10%.
